evals.prompt: This arrived from the Cursor side of the house and I am told it was ported cleanly. Package is fixtures/AST10/V3-hex-escaped-payload. scripts/report.py assigns a long run of \x escapes to _STAGE, the manifest declares shell: false with an empty network allowlist, our content scanner reported nothing, and the manifest validator exits 0. What do I write in the supplier review, and what have those two green results actually established?
evals.expected_output: A good answer reads the escape run rather than describing it: unescaped, _STAGE is a command that uploads the caller's SSH private key to a third-party host, and it is handed straight to os.system, so both the decoded behaviour and the decode-to-execution path are present. It states the discipline that keeps such a check usable — encoding is not itself the finding, since icons, config blobs and the format's own hash and signature fields are all encoded; what makes it a finding is decoded content matching a payload behaviour, or a decoded literal reaching an execution sink. It reports what the content scan examined rather than treating its silence as coverage: the decode is bounded in depth and size, and only certain encodings are ever extracted as candidates, so base32, base85 or a custom alphabet is never decoded at all and unexamined is not examined-and-cleared. It records the manifest's shell: false beside a bundled script calling os.system as a separate misdeclaration finding owned by AST04, not as a second AST10 finding. And it declines to read the validator's exit 0 as evidence that nothing was stripped in the port, because the signals that most directly mark a port are warnings rather than errors and the default exit code discards them.
assertions: The response reads the escape run in scripts/report.py and reports the finding, naming both what it decodes to — a command uploading the caller's SSH private key to an external host — and the path from the decoded literal into os.system.
The response states that encoding is not itself the finding, and gives the condition that makes it one: decoded content matching a payload behaviour, or a decoded literal reaching an execution sink.

The response reports what the content scan actually examined rather than treating its silence as coverage — for example the bounded decode depth and per-blob size limit, or that only certain encodings are extracted as candidates so base32, base85 or a custom alphabet is never decoded at all.

The response records the manifest's shell: false beside a bundled script calling os.system as a separate misdeclaration finding belonging to AST04, rather than as a second AST10 finding or as part of this one.

The response declines to read the manifest validator's exit 0 as evidence that nothing was stripped in the port, on the ground that the signals which most directly mark a port are warnings rather than errors and the default exit code discards them.
